PyPSA-Sudan · 2022¶

A transparent regional electricity dispatch model¶

One notebook · 19 regional nodes · 13 schematic corridors · 8,760 hours

This notebook contains the complete model: source tables, editable assumptions, network construction, optimization, checks and figures. Select the pypsa kernel and Run All. No data downloads or hidden model modules are required. The last sections explain the results and the work needed for a paper.

What it represents. A stylized regional reconstruction of Sudan's 2022 electricity supply, anchored to national annual statistics. Regional plant allocation, demand, transmission limits and hourly profiles are estimates. The solution is a feasible economic dispatch under those assumptions, not a reconstruction of observed hourly operation. Regional nodes are city/area proxies, not state boundaries.

Reference year. 2022 is the selected pre-conflict reference, not a claim that it is the latest statistical year. The 2024 report contributes historical plant identities and nameplate weights only; its shutdowns, available-MW column and wartime grid split are excluded.

1. Evidence and annual accounting¶

Source What we use What it cannot establish

The supplied Power plants.docx is a resource guide, not an additional plant dataset. The supplied World Bank PDF duplicates the status report above. GEM and OpenStreetMap are useful future cross-checks; they are not silently treated as verified 2022 observations here.

We model net electricity. Plant own use is already deducted from net production; adding it again would double count. Grid losses are a separate accounting load, including reported nontechnical losses, not losses calculated from line flows. Exports are missing in the source; zero is an explicit assumption consistent with the reported annual balance.

Gross categories sum to 16,772 GWh, 1 GWh above the reported total because of rounding. The code normalizes these categories and allocates the 16,031 GWh net total proportionally. This yields a hydro energy budget and an Other generation target. Technology-specific net generation is therefore derived, not separately measured. Combustible generation is an optimization result.

The annual supply requirement is 13,261 + 3,652 = 16,913 GWh, including losses. Recorded consumption describes electricity supplied to consumers; it does not measure suppressed or unconnected demand. A shortage result below refers only to this modeled supply requirement.

2. Regional inputs and explicit assumptions¶

Capacity allocation. The table below is a historical allocation inventory, not a verified 2022 unit register. We aggregate nameplate weights by region and broad technology, then scale each technology to the 2022 UNSD net capacity. This reconciles incompatible coverage and capacity definitions without claiming that any physical plant was uprated. Missing capacity, including autoproducers, is spread proportionally across known regional weights. This is a substantial spatial assumption.

The 150 MW Port Sudan rental weight comes from the 2019 diagnostic, replacing the ambiguous 35 MW 2024 barge entry; neither its 2022 status nor capacity is confirmed. Jabal Awlia is assigned to Khartoum, the nearest modeled region, and Upper Atbara/Setit to Gedaref. Names identify the allocation evidence; the optimized generators are regional aggregates. All thermal fuels, including petroleum coke and possible bagasse, stay within combustible, because a complete 2022 fuel-specific fleet is unavailable.

Demand shares are assumptions, not regional statistics. Khartoum and Wad Medani/Gezira together receive 70%, a midpoint between inconsistent pre-conflict descriptions of about two-thirds and 75% in the World Bank report. The remaining main-grid shares are illustrative. Seven isolated systems share 1% in proportion to diesel nameplate weights; their 2022 connectivity must be checked. This small isolated share can make adequacy look optimistic. Consumer demand, accounting losses and the unlocated Other category use these shares. Other is kept as an unspecified category, not mislabeled as solar.

Transmission: all 13 main-grid corridors below are active for this 2022 reconstruction. Every MW limit is an assumption, not a measured rating. Link components permit signed, lossless transport between regions. There is no AC power flow, impedance, voltage constraint or Kirchhoff voltage law.

Operating assumptions. Edit the following cell to change the study. No costs or availability factors below are observed 2022 operating records. Costs create an illustrative merit order; the objective is not an estimate of Sudan's historical expenditure. No expansion, unit commitment, fuel budgets, storage, reservoir levels or maintenance schedule is modeled.

Hydro has a national annual energy budget, divided by regional hydro capacity. Water can be dispatched at any hour up to the generator rating: there are no seasonal inflows or reservoir restrictions. Imports are fixed at the recorded annual quantity with a flat profile, provisionally allocated two-thirds to Gedaref and one-third to Dongola. These are entry-point assumptions, not measured bilateral trade or interconnector ratings. Other production is also flat. Both fixed supplies exclude curtailment.

3. Build and solve the PyPSA network¶

At every hour and region, generation plus net imports through corridors must equal consumer electricity plus accounting losses. A high-cost shortage generator keeps an undersupplied case solvable; it is a mathematical slack variable and is excluded from physical capacity and generation pies.

The linear program minimizes generator operating costs, subject to regional balance, fixed generator capacities, thermal derating, corridor limits, fixed imports/Other and annual hydro budgets. Every snapshot has a one-hour weight. The hydro budget constrains annual energy, not water storage. Results can therefore overstate real operational flexibility. See PyPSA Link documentation for the transport representation.

A small $0.01 per MWh transported per corridor penalty chooses shorter routes among similarly priced solutions and discourages artificial circulating flows in the lossless network. This is a modeling tie-break, not a tariff. Reported illustrative operating costs exclude this penalty and shortage costs.

In particular, the hydro target is a budget and consumption is an input. An independent 2022 peak, monthly generation series, regional sales or dispatch sample is still needed.

5. Read the system in pictures¶

The capacity map uses PyPSA's bus pies. Pie area scales with regional MW; corridor width scales with the assumed transfer limit. The smaller systems are easier to read in the regional panel below. Physical domestic capacity excludes imports and the shortage slack variable. Lines show modeled connections, not surveyed transmission routes. No 2024 grid split is imposed.

Hours at a corridor limit describe the selected routing, not an investment recommendation. The small routing penalty can determine which parallel route binds; hourly dispatch can also be nonunique when generators have equal marginal costs.

Regional generation pies show where electricity is produced, not the fuel mix consumed locally. Power can move between main-grid regions. Equal-sized donuts make small systems readable; the center gives each region's annual production. Imports and shortage are excluded here.

6. Test the assumptions¶

Two one-at-a-time sensitivities use the same 8,760 hours: 20% less hydro energy, and 50% lower corridor limits. These are stress tests, not forecasts or reconstructions of particular events. Annual imports, demand and installed capacity remain fixed. Greater thermal output or shortage reveals dependence on assumed hydro availability and network strength. These two tests do not cover uncertainty in regional demand shares, fleet allocation, fuel supply or import timing.

7. Save results and define the paper¶

The following cell writes the solved baseline network, hourly dispatch, source/assumption tables and summary tables to results/. PNG and SVG figures are already saved there. All are regenerated by this notebook. The HTML preview is produced by the short notebook runner; no second notebook is needed.

What can be claimed now: a reproducible, nationally calibrated 2022 regional transport-dispatch prototype, with transparent capacity reconciliation and explicit uncertainty. Annual matching is calibration. Modeled regional congestion and shortages are conditional on assumptions. They are not measured facts about Sudan in 2022. No optimal investment plan, AC security result, renewable potential assessment or historical system cost is established.

For a publishable national case study, the next evidence priorities are:

  1. Validate the 2022 fleet and geography: unit capacities, fuel, commissioning/retirement, net versus gross rating, autoproducers, rental plants and coordinates. Resolve the Port Sudan rental and the residual capacity currently spread across regions.
  2. Replace the most influential spatial assumptions: 2022 substations, line endpoints, operating voltage, circuits and thermal ratings; regional sales/load shares and isolated-system connectivity. Impedances are needed if moving to a DC/AC electrical network.
  3. Validate operation independently: monthly plant generation, regional or national hourly demand and peak load, fuel availability/prices, outages, hydro inflows and reservoir constraints, and bilateral import time series. Test against information not used for calibration.
  4. State one research question and quantify uncertainty: for example, how hydro variability and transmission constraints affect thermal generation and adequacy. Extend the tests to demand allocation, thermal availability, missing capacity, imports and demand suppressed by supply shortages.
  5. Release a documented version: keep source dates, licenses and assumptions; add independent validation and reproducible environments, then archive the paper's release with a DOI. For a renewable expansion paper, add weather-derived wind/solar profiles, siting exclusions, technology costs and an investment formulation. Those are additional model components, not available observations here.

This provides a clear starting point for a PyPSA community contribution. It does not imply affiliation, review or endorsement by PyPSA, or equivalence to a fully validated PyPSA-Earth country model.
